name: brainstorm
description: Multidisciplinary scientific panel: structure the submission (preprocessing reads everything and builds the structured input plus the per-file relation map; a separate reasoning stage then classifies it against the bundle input-type catalog — the single reference file that defines every type, its reviewing rubric, its output shape, and its outline — by the submitter's actual ask, never the domain narrative, offering a primary and an alternative reading plus the explicitly-or-unmistakably requested outputs, with a skippable countdown gate where the submitter confirms or revises the decision before any panel cost is incurred), annotate any attached code (a dedicated pass reads every code file and folds a one-line content summary into the shared file map), assemble an expert panel plus one deterministically woven interdisciplinary seat whose expertise is the space between the seated fields (a full member: it develops, is reviewed, and redevelops like every other seat), let every member work the submission in parallel in the shape the catalog maps its type to (delivering the chain of thought stepwise through the submit_step tool, assembled by the runtime), review each member chain of thought step by step — commentors (the interdisciplinary seat commenting through its own roster-aware skill on the crossings between fields) and a chain-grounded judge may fault the current step or any earlier one, an anonymized objection ledger carries every round's confirmed issues and each revision's runtime-computed change-set into the next round, and bounded redevelopment re-emits the complete chain with unaffected steps copied verbatim — audit the reviewed outputs across fields (novelty claims, contradictions, unexplored seams), then synthesize one final summary.

panelSize.description: Maximum number of seats the deterministic panel.select activity may produce.

maxAttachmentFiles.description: Ceiling on annotated attachment-inventory entries the file partition activities may emit.

maxPoolMembers.description: Ceiling on pool members the taxonomy matching and suggestion activities may process.

maxDepartments.description: Ceiling on departments the temporary experts bridge may emit (the experts tree itself allows at most 12).

maxSeats.description: Ceiling on panel seats after the interdisciplinary seat is woven in (panelSize plus one).

maxReviewRounds.description: Review rounds permitted at one walk position: the initial review plus at most (maxReviewRounds - 1) redevelopments. The ONLY place this budget is declared — the loop bound and the redevelop guard both derive from it.

steps.notes: Turn the raw submission into the structured input every downstream step reads. session.submission is the runtime-provided raw prompt plus attachment descriptors. Deliberately does NOT classify: the type decision is the next stage's job, made from this record.

Dedicated classification stage: a pure reasoning pass over the structured input and the attachment relation map (no file access) that decides the submission's type by the submitter's actual ask — explicit or implied — never by the domain narrative. Returns the primary reading, the strongest alternative (the two options the confirmation gate offers), the panel's chain-of-thought step count, the requested outputs including unmistakably implied asks, and the embedding input: the submission distilled into one paper-style title+abstract plus 3-8 single-concept facets, the clean retrieval text the semantic panel-assembly stage embeds and matches against the shared taxonomy.

Deterministic orchestrator step: fold the classifier's primary decision (type, cotSteps, requestedOutputs) into the structured input and REPLACE it, so every later task reads one merged record. The confirmation gate right after may overwrite type and requestedOutputs with the submitter's choice.

Optional checkpoint before any panel cost is incurred: the submitter confirms the classifier's primary reading, switches to the alternative or any other catalog type, and edits the requested outputs (select, add, remove). Left unanswered, the primary reading proceeds after a short countdown; unattended runtimes may auto-approve (skippable).

gate.title: Confirm the submission type
gate.prompt: Review how the submission was read before the panel is assembled. Approve the primary reading, or revise it: pick the alternative (or any listed type) and adjust the requested outputs the panel must answer. Left unanswered, the primary reading proceeds after a short countdown.

actions.description: Proceed with the classifier's primary reading as merged.
Proceed with a revised reading: a different catalog type and/or an edited requested-output list.

steps.notes: Deterministic orchestrator step: keep only the annotated files whose relation label is not NA. This list is the only file map any later model call receives.
Deterministic orchestrator step: the NA-labeled files as a separate audit artifact. Never bound into later model calls.

Deterministic orchestrator step: project the useful files to the code-labeled entries (code / implementation) and count them. The count gates the code-annotation pass; the projection is the exact list the annotator receives.
The code-annotation pass runs only when the submission actually carries code files; a code-free run skips it without a model call.

The code librarian reads EVERY code file through attachment-access and returns one line per file: what the file contains and how it bears on the input topic. The task schema pins the entry count and the exact paths, and the runtime re-checks completeness and order on write.

Deterministic orchestrator step: fold the annotator's summaries into the useful-file map by exact path match and REPLACE usefulFiles with the merged map, so every later task reads the annotated version. A summary naming an unknown path fails the run instead of being dropped silently.

Part one of the former decomposer: literature retrieval, full author enumeration, verbatim profile interests, term unification. Returns the expertise pool in which every member carries its origins (who stated it, on which paper) and its distinct-people count. No tree, no seating.

Deterministic orchestrator step, no model call: the HYBRID matching lane. Pillars first — one taxonomy_resolve round-trip per pool member against the LIVE shared taxonomy (exact name/alias match, untouchable). Then the semantic lane over the registry-served node-embedding index: still-unmatched terms are scored by cosine plus a small active-region boost warmed by the classifier's facets and the exact-match landings; an unambiguous score above the served threshold auto-matches, everything else carries its scored top candidates to the placer. Fail-safe: no served index or a conformance-failing local embedder turns the lane off and matching behaves exactly as before. Output carries every member's match or candidates, the unmatched projection for the placer, the lane status, and the taxonomy revision answered from.

Part two of the former decomposer: for the members deterministic matching could not resolve, read the whole latest shared taxonomy through the taxonomy-access capability and decide each member's canonical name and existing parent (or report it already present under another spelling). Decisions only — recording happens in the next step.

Deterministic orchestrator step: send a copy of the run's decision for every pool member (matched position, new placement, or already-present resolution) to the registry's append-only suggestion queue and record the receipt. Suggestions are queued, never applied here.

TEMPORARY until the pool-based seating design lands: deterministically fold matched positions and placement decisions into the legacy experts tree (the pool's literature grounding riding through) so panel.select and everything downstream keep working unchanged.

Provider-neutral deterministic runtime transform, no model call. The registered panel.select handler mixes every department/umbrella/topic node into one queue ordered by count x relevance, seats the highest while capacity remains, and prefers the more specific node when a descendant would seat itself; see the handler's own contract in catalog/activity-handlers.json for the authoritative algorithm.

Deterministic orchestrator step, no model call: append the panel's ONE interdisciplinary seat — a full member whose expertise is the space BETWEEN the seated fields, derived from the seated umbrella terms and marked seat=interdisciplinary. It develops, is reviewed, and redevelops like every other member; only its commenting skill differs (dispatched below). Skipped when the panel spans fewer than two distinct umbrellas.

Optional checkpoint before any member starts thinking. The automatic selection may only shrink here; the submitter may additionally seat explicit custom members (department, field, 1-3 focuses) — a host capability applied alongside the remove-only edit. Unattended runtimes may auto-approve (skippable), and the host may auto-approve an unanswered gate after a short countdown.

gate.title: Confirm the panel
gate.prompt: Review the seated panel before the brainstorm starts. Approve it as-is, remove seats to shrink it, or add your own custom seats (department, field, and 1-3 focuses). Left unanswered, the panel is approved as seated after a short countdown.

actions.description: Proceed with the seated panel as shown.
Remove one or more seats, then proceed with the remaining panel.

steps.notes: First pass: every member works the submission in parallel, producing the output shape the catalog maps input.type to, a chain of thought of exactly input.cotSteps steps, and (for shapes positioned against a literature map: paper, resolution, survey) a novelty statement.
Review every member's chain of thought, one member at a time.

body.notes: Walk the member's chain step by step. The chain's LENGTH is invariant: a redevelopment re-emits the complete chain (unaffected steps verbatim) but never changes the step count, so this loop runs exactly input.cotSteps times. Advancing past a position means no demonstrable flaw currently stands anywhere in steps 1..position.

One iteration = one review round at the current walk position: gather comments (each targeting the current step or any earlier one), judge over the actual chain, and redevelop if the judge did not Pass. Bounded by the maxReviewRounds param — the loop compiles to that param's declared ceiling and exits on the runtime-stamped reviews[member.id].finalRound flag, so the budget is declared in exactly ONE place. onExhausted=proceed is the backstop forced pass. reviews[member.id].allowedVerdicts is computed by the runtime from bundle.verdicts.sequencing and this position's previous round (a Build may not immediately follow a Build); reviews[member.id].history is the seat's anonymized objection ledger, refreshed every round. All review state is seat-qualified so two members' walks never collide.

steps.notes: Every panel member except the thinker comments in parallel. Commentors see chain steps 1..stepIndex (never the developed paper) plus the anonymized objection ledger, and may fault the current step or any earlier one — the comment's `step` field names the target. The panel's interdisciplinary seat comments through its own skill (roster-aware, covering the areas between the seated fields); every disciplinary seat uses the standard commentor skill.

then.notes: The interdisciplinary seat's comment: same verdicts, same evidence discipline, but its field is the space between the seated members — it receives the full roster and reviews the crossings between fields, never re-litigating a point inside one field's own lane.

steps.notes: One judgement over all comments of this round, grounded in the chain itself: the judge reads steps 1..stepIndex, verifies every comment against the actual step text, checks the ledger's earlier objections against the last revision's change-set, and returns the de-duplicated issues[] repair signal.

Redevelop only when the judge did not Pass AND a redevelopment budget remains. Both conditions read runtime state — the round budget lives solely in the maxReviewRounds param, never as a literal here.

then.notes: The reviser re-emits the COMPLETE chain through submit_step: steps the confirmed issues implicate (at any position) are rewritten, every unaffected step is copied verbatim, and the paper and novelty are replaced. The runtime — never the model — computes the touched/untouched change-set by exact comparison, records it in the ledger, and the next round re-reviews at the same walk position with that change-set in view.

steps.notes: Sequential integration audit after review: one auditor reads every member's finished output (the chains never reach it, by construction), verifies each novelty claim across fields, and maps contradictions and unexplored seams between the seats. Advisory input to the chair.
Rapporteur step. The bind projects each idea to its output and novelty statement only — the chain of thought never reaches the chair, by construction.
